gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could open states how many amp-hours a day each front-and-rear camera takes from the car battery while parked (about 8 Ah for the Vantrue S1 Pro Max 4K+4K in low-bitrate parking against under 1 Ah for the Viofo A329S in its low-power impact mode), or that the 4K+4K Vantrue keeps about 12 hours of both-camera footage per 256 GB only because it writes about 0.10 bit per front pixel against the Viofo A229 Pro's 0.23.
standout_why: Compared against thecargearguide's A229 Plus/Pro/A329S page (cited), thecargearguide's front-and-rear page, and Product Bible's front-and-rear and Viofo-models pages. The cited thecargearguide page already gives front/rear bitrates and GB per hour for the three Viofos, so hours-per-card for those is one division away. Product Bible gives 'about six days of 3-hour drives on 512GB' for the A329S. thecargearguide's front-and-rear page quotes Vortex Radar's parking durations for Thinkware and BlackVue. None of them has a per-day battery draw for the Viofo A229 series or the Vantrue, any bitrate or hours-per-card figure for a 4K+4K kit, or bits per pixel. Capped at 1 because two cited pages, Vortex Radar (HTTP 403) and Car and Driver (fetch blocked), could not be opened, and Vortex Radar is known for parking-power measurements.
decides: It confirms ChatGPT's order rather than changing it. The A329S is the pick for anyone who parks for days: under 1 Ah a day in low-power impact mode against 8-12 Ah a day for low-bitrate recording on the others. The A229 Pro 2CH is the stronger front-evidence camera per dollar: its 4K front gets 57 Mb/s against 23.8 Mb/s on the Vantrue. Our Vantrue S1 Pro Max 4K+4K honestly wins a narrower segment: the only candidate here with a 4K rear, a 1 TB card limit and roughly 12 hours of loop per 256 GB (about 47 hours on 1 TB), at $239.99 against $349.99 for the A229 Pro at Viofo's store. The page should say that the longer loop comes from heavier compression, not present it as a free win.

findings.label: Measured bitrate with front and rear both recording
findings.value: 23.8 Mb/s front + 23.8 Mb/s rear at 3840x2160 30 fps each; front alone 23.8 Mb/s, raised to 31.9 Mb/s by a late-2025 firmware
findings.source_title: Reviewing and Testing the Vantrue S1 Pro Max (DashCamTalk forum, EricSan, post #1)
findings.note: EricSan's measurement, 2-channel: front (road ahead) + rear (road behind). Whether the 31.9 Mb/s firmware figure also applies when both cameras record is not stated in the text I read.

findings.label: Derived: storage use and hours of both-camera footage before the loop overwrites
findings.value: 21.4 GB per hour; about 12.0 hours per 256 GB; about 46.7 hours on the 1 TB maximum card
findings.source_title: Reviewing and Testing the Vantrue S1 Pro Max (DashCamTalk forum, EricSan, post #1)
findings.note: (23.8 + 23.8) Mb/s x 0.45 GB/h per Mb/s = 21.4 GB/h; 256 / 21.4 = 12.0 h; 1000 / 21.4 = 46.7 h. The 1 TB limit is from post #1 ('Supports up to 1TB microSD Card'). Ignores audio, locked files and formatting overhead. If the front runs at 31.9 Mb/s with both recording: 55.7 x 0.45 = 25.1 GB/h, 10.2 h per 256 GB.

findings.label: Measured front bitrate in the front + rear configuration
findings.value: 57 Mb/s front in 1-channel and 2-channel (rear) configurations; drops to about 35 Mb/s with an interior camera attached
findings.source_title: DashCamTalk forum, A229 Plus / A229 Pro thread (Chuck McCoy, post #133, Nov 9 2023)
findings.note: A forum member's measurement, not the maker's figure. The rear bitrate is not on this page.

findings.label: Derived: bits per pixel on the 4K front camera at 30 fps (how hard each camera compresses)
findings.value: Viofo A229 Pro 0.229 bit/pixel; Vantrue S1 Pro Max 0.096 bit/pixel (0.128 at the 31.9 Mb/s firmware figure)
findings.source_title: DashCamTalk forum, A229 Plus / A229 Pro thread (Chuck McCoy, post #133); Vantrue input from EricSan's S1 Pro Max thread, post #1
findings.note: Bitrate / (3840 x 2160 x 30 = 248.8 million pixels per second): 57 / 248.8 = 0.229; 23.8 / 248.8 = 0.096; 31.9 / 248.8 = 0.128. The Viofo spends about 2.4 times the bits per front pixel (57 / 23.8). Codec for each was not confirmed on a page I opened today, so treat this as a compression-budget comparison, not a detail test.

findings.label: Measured power draw
findings.value: 8.7 W driving with both cameras (screen and Wi-Fi on); 4.9 W front camera alone with GPS; 4.1-4.2 W in Low Bit Rate parking mode (1080p 15 fps, screen off)
findings.source_title: Reviewing and Testing the Vantrue S1 Pro Max (DashCamTalk forum, EricSan, posts #15 and #19, Jun 22-23 2025)
findings.note: EricSan measured with a multimeter inline on the hardwire kit's negative lead (Vantrue VP03 (II) kit), averaging at least 30 seconds; parking figures include the hardwire kit. He notes the manual lists 6 W. Collision-detection parking wakes in about 2.3 s (Quick Start) or about 10 s (Power Saving) and records 30 s; no wattage for those modes is in the text.

findings.note: 4.2 W x 24 h = 100.8 Wh; 100.8 / 12.6 V = 8.0 Ah. Both cameras, screen off.

findings.label: Maker's low-power parking draw and derived battery draw per 24 hours parked
findings.value: under 40 mA at 12.6 V (under 0.50 W) in Low Power Impact Detection; cameras wake and record in under 2 seconds; under 0.96 Ah per day parked
findings.source_title: VIOFO A329S 2CH 4K 60FPS+2K HDR Dash Cam (viofo.com product listing)
findings.note: 0.040 A x 24 h = 0.96 Ah; 0.040 A x 12.6 V = 0.50 W. This is Viofo's claim, read from the listing text returned by the store search; the product page itself returned HTTP 429 on a second read. The mode records only after an impact, so it is not comparable footage to low-bitrate recording. Front IMX678 4K 60 fps + rear IMX675 2K, per the same listing.
